learning_outcomes.text: Apply complex supervised learning techniques using an appropriate algorithm depending on the type of problem.
Be able to identify problems where the data distribution changes and adapt models to improve their accuracy.
Understand the concepts of reinforcement learning and know how to use these types of algorithms to solve real applications.
Know how to apply unsupervised learning techniques for knowledge extraction.
Know the basic algorithms for anomaly detection.
Know semi-supervised learning techniques to address applications where unlabeled data abounds.

Students should be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.

Students should have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students should be able to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical and signal processing methods.

Possess experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to design experiments and describe, analyze, evaluate and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to solve problems.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Identify opportunities for innovative data-oriented applications in continuously evolving technological environments.
Ability to clearly and convincingly express data processing results both in writing and orally.
Use the most appropriate techniques for data preprocessing and visualization, including dimensionality reduction techniques, in order to facilitate their analysis and communication.
Construction of machine learning systems using basic and advanced techniques, to build intelligent systems from data sets.

syllabus_topics: Problems with changes in data distribution

assessment_methods.method: Virtual Campus Activities (ACV): online theoretical tests and practical exercises
Attendance / participation in seminars and tutorials, including online activities (PAR): attendance and active participation in laboratory practices and other course activities

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the final grade is calculated as Note = ACV * 0.15 + PAR * 0.05 + TE * 0.40 + PR * 0.40. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required for both the Theoretical Exam (TE) and the Practical Exam (PR); if either is below 4, the final grade will be the minimum of 4 and the calculated note. To pass, a final grade of 5 or higher out of 10 is required. If the total weight of assessed activities completed by the student is less than 50%, the final grade will be “No Presentado”. For extraordinary assessments, the grade is calculated as Note = TE * 0.50 + PR * 0.50, with a minimum of 4 points required in both exams. Students can carry over a score of 4 or higher from a previous exam in the same course and year.
